name: Q and Not U
label: Dischord
lede: Seven years, three albums, thirty-one kids in primary colors on one album cover, and a D.C. punk band that decided the crowd should dance.

eras.title: A new band from the ashes of a few old ones
eras.text: By the late '90s the D.C. scene that built Dischord had grown up, and Q and Not U were among the first of the next generation to get noticed. They formed out of several broken-up bands and spent their first year in basements and living rooms.

years.h: Q and Not U form: four guys, three voices
years.p: Q and Not U: [[Chris Richards|0065280c-f561-4035-aa65-e9927988d72e]] and [[Harris Klahr|c788433e-623b-4e6c-8998-7c372b8d51b7]] on guitars and vocals, [[John Davis|4729cedd-e42f-4836-8332-6cd316e60268]] on drums and vocals, Matt Borlik on bass.

years.h: Q and Not U's first shows
years.p: Dischord dates Q and Not U's first live dates to November 1998, a few months after they started practicing.

years.h: Q and Not U's house-show summer
years.p: A string of Q and Not U house shows becomes what the Washington City Paper calls the band's coming-out party. [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] takes notice, drawn to their musical language and the tight crowd forming around them.

eras.title: Thirty-one punks in primary colors
eras.text: Dischord put them out, Ian MacKaye produced them, and the cover of No Kill No Beep Beep became a group portrait of D.C. punk's next wave. Then came the long tours, and bassist Matt Borlik was out.

years.h: Hot and Informed · Dischord No. 123.5
years.p: Q and Not U's first single, a joint release by Dischord and DeSoto.

q: We were just waiting for some custodian to bust us.
years.h: The No Kill No Beep Beep cover shoot: 31 kids
years.p: Chris Richards gathers 31 young D.C. punks, mostly under 25, dressed in red, yellow and blue, in a George Washington University seminar room. Shawn Brackbill shoots the Q and Not U album cover.
years.xp: The shoot wasn't exactly sanctioned. Richards remembered the whole room half expecting to be thrown out.

years.h: No Kill No Beep Beep · Dischord No. 123
years.p: Q and Not U's debut, produced by Ian MacKaye at [[Don Zientara|a495882b-4585-4295-9269-e30c63f279fe]]'s Inner Ear in about ten days: jagged guitars, three voices trading lines, and a rhythm section built to make people move.
years.xp: The band had grown up on Dischord records and asked MacKaye to work with them.

years.h: Live in Washington DC, November 26, 2000
Q and Not U tour with friends
years.p: Q and Not U play long tours alongside [[Engine Down|65c54877-7b81-4cb1-8e6b-dc14fbec8b43]], [[Milemarker|151cbcfa-4618-4f26-a769-f15d33743262]], [[Ted Leo and the Pharmacists|31095622-5a1e-4f22-8ad1-b08eb6255f37]] and [[El Guapo|be23bf0a-67c6-4b2f-ba2a-89d983f5ebdd]].

years.h: Matt Borlik out of Q and Not U, and nobody replaces him
years.p: After two years of touring, Q and Not U dismiss bassist Matt Borlik, as Wikipedia puts it, and carry on as a three-piece. Chris Richards takes over the bass parts.

eras.title: Three people, more sounds
eras.text: Down to a trio, Q and Not U got stranger and bolder rather than smaller. They toured the U.S., Europe, Canada and Japan, and kept Dischord supplied with records.

years.h: On Play Patterns · Dischord No. 132
years.p: Q and Not U's first release as a trio.

years.h: Different Damage · Dischord No. 133
years.p: Q and Not U's second album, made without a dedicated bass player. Chris Richards covers bass alongside guitar and vocals.

years.h: X-Polynation / Book of Flags single
years.p: Two Q and Not U songs on a Dischord single (No. 141), a year before their last album, Power.

eras.title: Make them dance, then stop
eras.text: Power, the last album, went hard at the one thing D.C. punk shows rarely had: dancing. A year later Q and Not U called it off while they were still climbing, with a statement that sounded more like a thank-you than a breakup.

years.big: A D.C. punk band that wanted you dancing.
q: No one ever danced at shows, so we wanted something that got people excited.
years.h: Power, Q and Not U's last album · Dischord No. 143
years.p: Q and Not U's third and final album, and the one they built most deliberately for dancing.
years.xp: Drummer John Davis has said the goal was straightforward: get people moving at shows where nobody moved.

years.h: Live at the YWCA, Cambridge, 2004
Q and Not U announce their breakup
years.p: After seven years, Q and Not U say they have reached their shared goals and it's a natural time to stop. They add that they hope to play together again someday.

years.h: Q and Not U play Coney Island's Siren Festival
years.p: Nine days after announcing the breakup, Q and Not U play the Siren Music Festival on the Coney Island boardwalk, one of their last shows outside D.C.

years.cap: Q and Not U · via Discogs
years.h: Q and Not U play a free show at Fort Reno
years.p: A Monday night Q and Not U gig at Fort Reno, D.C.'s free summer concert series in the park, booked before the breakup news, becomes one of the goodbyes.

years.h: Q and Not U's Wonderful People remix EP
years.p: A Q and Not U remix EP comes out as the band winds down.

years.cap: Q and Not U · via Discogs
years.h: Q and Not U's farewell at the Black Cat
years.p: After finishing their touring commitments, Q and Not U close with two nights at the Black Cat on 14th Street, a Thursday and a Friday. Fans who were there told Brooklyn Vegan the last song was Soft Pyramids.
years.xp: The Fort Reno show had been booked well before the July announcement; the Black Cat dates were added afterward as the proper send-off.

eras.title: The critic and the Paint Branch
eras.text: The three went their own ways: John Davis into pop with Georgie James and later Title Tracks, Harris Klahr into his own projects in New York, and Chris Richards into solo records as Ris Paul Ric and, eventually, the Washington Post. Richards and Davis ended up in a band together again.

years.h: Chris Richards joins the Washington Post
years.p: Q and Not U's guitarist, bassist and cover-shoot organizer becomes the Post's pop music critic.

years.h: Chris Richards and John Davis form [[Paint Branch|a440caa0-3fa8-4c39-9cd7-8fa0dffedd6e]]
years.p: The two former Q and Not U members start a new band, active through 2014 and listed on Dischord's Q and Not U page.

eras.title: The drummer keeps the files
eras.text: Q and Not U drummer John Davis became the keeper of the scene's paper trail: archivist at the University of Maryland, where D.C. punk's zines and flyers live, and then its historian.

years.h: John Davis, D.C. punk archivist
years.p: The Washington Post profiles Q and Not U drummer John Davis keeping D.C. punk alive at a University of Maryland library, where he looks after the scene's collected papers.

years.h: John Davis's book, Keep Your Ear to the Ground
years.p: John Davis publishes a history of D.C. punk fanzines, and launches it at Politics and Prose in conversation with [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]], who produced Q and Not U's first album.
